mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on matches where the possession differential between the two sides exceeds a threshold (e.g., Team B holds >55% possession), then measure whether Team A's foul rate is elevated relative to its unconditional average. This is a joint two-observable interaction, not a single-observable band.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Team A's foul production rises as Team B's possession share increases beyond a threshold, reflecting a suppression-and-foul dynamic that saturates at high possession differentials.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's dominant possession profile (historically ~61%) combined with Team A's high foul rate (historically ~17.2 fouls/match, elevated away at ~18.3) creates a joint condition where Team A's foul production rises as a function of Team B's possession dominance — i.e., the interaction between one team's possession share and the opposing team's foul rate jointly predicts foul volume beyond what either observable alone captures.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires jointly conditioning on two distinct observables from two different teams simultaneously (Team B's possession AND Team A's foul rate), which cannot be reduced to a single observable with one coarse band. It is an asymmetric cross-team interaction.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on matches where Team B's possession exceeds a threshold (e.g., >55%), then measure the joint distribution of Team A corners conceded and Team B corners produced. Compare against each team's unconditional corner averages to test whether the possession-corner relationship is super-additive.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Total corner volume rises with Team B's possession dominance, with Team A's corners-against and Team B's corners-for both elevated above their unconditional means when possession differential is large.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's high possession share jointly interacts with Team A's corner kick concession rate: when Team B dominates possession, Team A concedes significantly more corners than its unconditional average, while Team B's corner production is also elevated — creating a compounding corner-volume effect driven by the joint possession-corner relationship across both teams.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a joint two-observable, two-team interaction (possession differential AND corner production/concession for both sides simultaneously), not reducible to a single observable with one band. The super-additive structure requires measuring both observables together.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Split goals by half for both teams simultaneously. Condition on the joint first-half vs. second-half goal rates for both Team A (FOR and AGAINST) and Team B (FOR and AGAINST) to test whether the second half produces a disproportionate share of total goals relative to competition context norms.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Second-half goal volume for both teams combined is elevated relative to first-half volume, and this asymmetry is more pronounced than the competition-context baseline implies.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B exhibits a pronounced within-match goal-scoring asymmetry: its second-half goal rate (~1.015/match) is substantially higher than its first-half rate (~0.662/match), while Team A's goals-against are also back-loaded (first-half ~0.667, second-half ~0.750). The joint half-level scoring profiles of both teams — measured simultaneously — test whether the second-half goal environment is structurally elevated beyond what full-match averages imply.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires jointly conditioning on half-level splits for both teams' FOR and AGAINST goal rates simultaneously, comparing the within-match state structure across both sides — not a single observable with one band. The half-level resolution and cross-team joint structure make it structurally richer.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly condition on: (1) Team A's second-half card rate and foul rate, (2) Team B's second-half card rate and possession dominance, and (3) competition context second-half card norm. Test whether the combined second-half card environment when a high-fouling team faces a possession-dominant team exceeds what either team's individual card rate or the competition norm predicts.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Second-half total cards are elevated above competition context norms when a high-fouling team (Team A) faces a possession-dominant team (Team B), with the joint effect exceeding the sum of individual team deviations from the norm.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's second-half card accumulation (cards_2h FOR ~1.723/match) combined with Team A's second-half card accumulation (cards_2h FOR ~2.389/match) — both measured against the competition context second-half card norm (~1.35/match) — tests whether the joint second-half disciplinary environment in this specific matchup is structurally elevated above competition norms, driven by the interaction of Team A's high foul rate and Team B's possession-dominant style creating late-match friction.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This involves three observables jointly (cards_2h, fouls, possession), two teams' second-half profiles simultaneously, and a within-match state (second half) — not reducible to any single observable with one band or a simple home/away split.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Compute the ratio of shots_on_target to shots for Team B (FOR) and for Team A (AGAINST) separately, then jointly condition on whether Team B's shot-conversion-to-target ratio is suppressed when facing teams with Team A's defensive shot-filtering profile. Test whether the joint ratio structure predicts shots_on_target volume better than either team's raw shots or shots_on_target average alone.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Team B's shots-on-target production is suppressed relative to its raw shot volume when facing a team (Team A) whose shots-on-target-against rate is below the competition norm, indicating a non-linear filtering effect that saturates as defensive quality improves.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's shot-to-shots-on-target conversion ratio (shots ~14.9, shots_on_target ~4.86, all-prior) versus Team A's shots-against-to-shots-on-target-against ratio (shots_against ~12.4, shots_on_target_against ~3.97) jointly characterize the shot quality / defensive filtering interaction: when Team B's volume shooting meets Team A's relatively efficient shot-suppression, the net shots-on-target environment may be suppressed relative to what Team B's raw shot volume alone implies. This tests a non-linear, ratio-based relationship between two observables across both teams.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a ratio/non-linear relationship between two distinct observables (shots and shots_on_target) measured asymmetrically across both teams — Team B's offensive conversion ratio interacting with Team A's defensive filtering ratio. It cannot be reduced to a single observable with one band.
